Following the March 1984 release of the romantic comedy *Splash*—in which Daryl Hannah's mermaid character chooses her name from a Madison Avenue street sign—"Madison" transformed from a rare male surname (just **42** baby girls in 1984) into a cultural phenomenon. Fueled by the 1990s surname-as-first-name trend, TV characters, and eventually the first generation of celebrity Madisons born after *Splash*, the name peaked at **22,166** girls (#2 in the U.S.) in **2001**.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5

library(tidyverse)

# Read the SSA baby names dataset (1984–2025)
madison_df <- read_csv("ssa-baby-names.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(name == "Madison", year >= 1984) |>
  mutate(sex = recode(sex, "F" = "Female", "M" = "Male"))

# Build 5-pointed star polygons in data coordinates for the plot background
make_star <- function(cx, cy, r_x = 0.55, r_y = 650, id = 1, col = "#f783ac") {
  angles <- seq(pi / 2, pi / 2 + 2 * pi, length.out = 11)[-11]
  radii <- rep(c(1, 0.42), 5)
  tibble(
    id = id,
    col = col,
    x = cx + r_x * radii * cos(angles),
    y = cy + r_y * radii * sin(angles)
  )
}

star_centers <- tibble(
  cx = c(1985.2, 1988.0, 1992.0, 1995.2, 2004.2, 2008.2, 2012.2, 2016.0, 2021.2, 2024.3,
         1986.2, 1991.2, 2015.0, 2020.2, 2023.2, 2010.2, 2018.0, 2024.8),
  cy = c(24500, 17500, 25000, 26500, 27000, 18500, 26200, 21000, 25200, 19500,
         14200, 16000, 5200, 11500, 9500, 5500, 3800, 13500),
  scale = rep(c(1.1, 0.85, 1.0), 6),
  col = rep(c("#f783ac", "#b197fc", "#e599f7", "#faa2c1", "#d0bfff", "#ff85c0"), 3)
)

bg_stars <- pmap_dfr(
  list(star_centers$cx, star_centers$cy, star_centers$scale, seq_len(nrow(star_centers)), star_centers$col),
  \(cx, cy, sc, id, col) make_star(cx, cy, r_x = 0.55 * sc, r_y = 680 * sc, id = id, col = col)
)

bg_hearts <- tibble(
  x = c(1986.8, 1994.0, 2003.0, 2009.5, 2014.2, 2019.5, 2022.8),
  y = c(21500, 23200, 8200, 25500, 20500, 22500, 16200),
  col = c("#f783ac", "#b197fc", "#f783ac", "#e599f7", "#b197fc", "#ff85c0", "#d0bfff")
)

# Cultural & celebrity events that shaped the popularity of "Madison"
events <- tibble(
  year = c(1984, 1990, 1997, 2001, 2005, 2013),
  count = c(42, 1407, 15189, 22166, 19578, 10605),
  label_x = c(1988.8, 1988.8, 1993.2, 2000.0, 2011.5, 2018.5),
  label_y = c(4300, 11200, 19600, 26000, 22800, 15200),
  event_label = c(
    "1984: Movie 'Splash' premieres\nMermaid picks name from Madison Ave\n(only 42 girls in 1984 → 301 in 1985)",
    "1990: 90s Surname Trend\nRises alongside Taylor & Jordan\n(1,407 girls)",
    "1997: Enters U.S. Top 10\nJumps to #10 most popular girl name\n(15,189 girls)",
    "2001 All-Time Peak: 22,166 girls (#2 in U.S.)\n'Cardcaptors' ('Madison Taylor') airs on TV",
    "2005: 'Suite Life of Zack & Cody'\nAshley Tisdale's 'Maddie' fuels nickname craze\n(19,578 girls)",
    "2013: 1st-Gen Madisons Become Stars\nMadison Beer, Madison Keys & Disney's\n'Liv and Maddie' debut (10,605 girls)"
  )
)

madison_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = count, color = sex, fill = sex)) +
  # Soft pink & purple 5-pointed stars and hearts in the background sky
  geom_polygon(
    data = bg_stars,
    aes(x = x, y = y, group = id),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = bg_stars$col,
    color = "#a61e4d",
    linewidth = 0.2,
    alpha = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = bg_hearts,
    aes(x = x, y = y),
    label = "♥",
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = bg_hearts$col,
    size = 6,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.28, position = "identity") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
  # Dashed leader lines connecting points on the curve to event callouts
  geom_segment(
    data = events,
    aes(x = year, y = count, xend = label_x, yend = label_y),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#c2255c",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  # Highlight milestone points on the Female curve
  geom_point(
    data = events,
    aes(x = year, y = count),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#a61e4d",
    fill = "#fff0f6",
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.5,
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  # Callout boxes for each cultural milestone
  geom_label(
    data = events,
    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = event_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = "#fff0f6",
    color = "#862e9c",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.0,
    label.padding = unit(0.35, "lines"),
    label.r = unit(0.25, "lines")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Female" = "#d63384", "Male" = "#9775fa")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Female" = "#f783ac", "Male" = "#d0bfff")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1985, 2025, by = 5), limits = c(1983, 2026)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    limits = c(0, 28000)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "♥ How Pop Culture Turned 'Madison' Into an Iconic Girls' Name (1984–2025) ♥",
    subtitle = "Annual U.S. births with key movies, TV shows, and celebrity milestones marked",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Babies",
    color = "Sex",
    fill = "Sex",
    caption = "♥ Source: U.S. Social Security Administration (1984–2025) ♥"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#fff9fb", color = "#e599f7", linewidth = 2),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#fff9fb", color = NA),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#f3d9fa", linetype = "dotted"),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#862e9c", face = "bold", size = 13.5, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#a61e4d", size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 14, 14, 14),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```
